audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Balak, Balaam, donkey, and angelic-road narrative tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Moabite fear, curse-for-hire embassy, Balaam's Divine consultation, permission/anger tension, angel as adversary, speaking donkey, animal mistreatment, restricted speech, and Balak's first sacrificial sites.

verses.restored: Children of Israel set out and camped in plains of Moab, across Jordan from Jericho.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel set forward, and pitched in the plains of Moab on this side Jordan by Jericho.

modern.text: Then the Israelites traveled on and camped in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho.

modern.text: and Moab was terrified of the people because they were numerous. Indeed, Moab dreaded the Israelites.

modern.text: So the Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “This horde will devour everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” Since Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time,

verses.restored: Now, please, come curse this people for me, for it is mightier than I. Perhaps I will be able to strike it and drive it from land, for I know that whom you bless is blessed and whom you curse is cursed.

familiar.text: Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: peradventure I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land: for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.

modern.text: So please come now and put a curse on this people, because they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I may be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land; for I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.”

modern.text: The elders of Moab and Midian departed with the fees for divination in hand. They came to Balaam and relayed to him the words of Balak.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ זִקְנֵ֤י מוֹאָב֙ וְזִקְנֵ֣י מִדְיָ֔ן וּקְסָמִ֖ים בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו דִּבְרֵ֥י בָלָֽק

modern.text: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and I will give you the answer that the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.

modern.text: But Balaam replied to the servants of Balak, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything small or great to go beyond the command of the LORD my God.

familiar.text: And God came unto Balaam at night, and said unto him, If the men come to call thee, rise up, and go with them; but yet the word which I shall say unto thee, that shalt thou do.

modern.text: Then God’s anger was kindled because Balaam was going along, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

modern.text: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the path and went into a field. So Balaam beat her to return her to the path.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD went further, and stood in a narrow place, where was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.

modern.text: And the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn to the right or left.

original.text: וַיּ֥וֹסֶף מַלְאַךְ יְהוָ֖ה עֲב֑וֹר וַֽיַּעֲמֹד֙ בְּמָק֣וֹם צָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֛ר אֵֽין דֶּ֥רֶךְ לִנְט֖וֹת יָמִ֥ין וּשְׂמֹֽאול

verses.restored: Donkey saw messenger of YHWH and lay down under Balaam; anger of Balaam burned, and he struck donkey with staff.

familiar.text: And when the ass saw the angel of the LORD, she fell down under Balaam: and Balaam’s anger was kindled, and he smote the ass with a staff.

modern.text: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam, and he became furious and beat her with his staff.

original.text: וַתֵּ֤רֶא הָֽאָתוֹן֙ אֶת מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּרְבַּ֖ץ תַּ֣חַת בִּלְעָ֑ם וַיִּֽחַר אַ֣ף בִּלְעָ֔ם וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת הָאָת֖וֹן בַּמַּקֵּֽל

verses.restored: YHWH opened mouth of donkey, and she said to Balaam, What have I done to you, that you struck me these three times?

familiar.text: And the LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?

modern.text: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”

original.text: וַיִּפְתַּ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה אֶת פִּ֣י הָאָת֑וֹן וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לְבִלְעָם֙ מֶה עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי לְךָ֔ כִּ֣י הִכִּיתַ֔נִי זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֥שׁ רְגָלִֽים

verses.restored: Balaam said to donkey, Because you made a fool of me! If only there were sword in my hand, for now I would kill you.

familiar.text: And Balaam said unto the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: I would there were a sword in mine hand, for now would I kill thee.

modern.text: Balaam answered the donkey, “You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר בִּלְעָם֙ לָֽאָת֔וֹן כִּ֥י הִתְעַלַּ֖לְתְּ בִּ֑י ל֤וּ יֶשׁ חֶ֨רֶב֙ בְּיָדִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה הֲרַגְתִּֽיךְ

verses.restored: Donkey said to Balaam, Am I not your donkey, upon whom you have ridden from your beginning until this day? Have I ever been accustomed to do thus to you? And he said, No.

familiar.text: And the ass said unto Balaam, Am not I thine ass, upon which thou hast ridden ever since I was thine unto this day? was I ever wont to do so unto thee? And he said, Nay.

modern.text: But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not the donkey you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” “No,” he replied.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר הָאָת֜וֹן אֶל בִּלְעָ֗ם הֲלוֹא֩ אָנֹכִ֨י אֲתֹֽנְךָ֜ אֲשֶׁר רָכַ֣בְתָּ עָלַ֗י מֵעֽוֹדְךָ֙ עַד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה הַֽהַסְכֵּ֣ן הִסְכַּ֔נְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְךָ֖ כֹּ֑ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹֽא

verses.restored: YHWH uncovered eyes of Balaam, and he saw messenger of YHWH standing in road with drawn sword in his hand; he bowed and fell upon his face.

familiar.text: Then the LORD opened the eyes of Balaam, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and he bowed down his head, and fell flat on his face.

modern.text: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.

original.text: וַיְגַ֣ל יְהוָה֮ אֶת עֵינֵ֣י בִלְעָם֒ וַיַּ֞רְא אֶת מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ נִצָּ֣ב בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְחַרְבּ֥וֹ שְׁלֻפָ֖ה בְּיָד֑וֹ וַיִּקֹּ֥ד וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לְאַפָּֽיו

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH said to him, Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I came out as adversary, for your way is reckless/perverse before me.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto him, Wherefore hast thou smitten thine ass these three times? behold, I went out to withstand thee, because thy way is perverse before me:

modern.text: The angel of the LORD asked him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה עַל מָ֗ה הִכִּ֨יתָ֙ אֶת אֲתֹ֣נְךָ֔ זֶ֖ה שָׁל֣וֹשׁ רְגָלִ֑ים הִנֵּ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ יָצָ֣אתִי לְשָׂטָ֔ן כִּֽי יָרַ֥ט הַדֶּ֖רֶךְ לְנֶגְדִּֽי

verses.restored: Donkey saw me and turned aside before me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, surely now I would have killed you and kept her alive.

familiar.text: And the ass saw me, and turned from me these three times: unless she had turned from me, surely now also I had slain thee, and saved her alive.

modern.text: The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, then by now I would surely have killed you and let her live.”

original.text: וַתִּרְאַ֨נִי֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֵּ֣ט לְפָנַ֔י זֶ֖ה שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֑ים אוּלַי֙ נָטְתָ֣ה מִפָּנַ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֛ה גַּם אֹתְכָ֥ה הָרַ֖גְתִּי וְאוֹתָ֥הּ הֶחֱיֵֽיתִי

verses.restored: Balaam said to messenger of YHWH, I have sinned/misaligned, for I did not know you were stationed before me in road. Now, if it is evil in your eyes, I will return.

familiar.text: And Balaam said unto the angel of the LORD, I have sinned; for I knew not that thou stoodest in the way against me: now therefore, if it displease thee, I will get me back again.

modern.text: “I have sinned,” Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me. And now, if this is displeasing in your sight, I will go back home.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם אֶל מַלְאַ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ חָטָ֔אתִי כִּ֚י לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י אַתָּ֛ה נִצָּ֥ב לִקְרָאתִ֖י בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְעַתָּ֛ה אִם רַ֥ע בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ אָשׁ֥וּבָה לִּֽי

verses.restored: Messenger of YHWH said to Balaam, Go with men, but only word that I speak to you, that you shall speak. So Balaam went with leaders of Balak.

familiar.text: And the angel of the LORD said unto Balaam, Go with the men: but only the word that I shall speak unto thee, that thou shalt speak. So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.

modern.text: But the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you are to speak only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מַלְאַ֨ךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֶל בִּלְעָ֗ם לֵ֚ךְ עִם הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְאֶ֗פֶס אֶת הַדָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר אֲדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ אֹת֣וֹ תְדַבֵּ֑ר וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בִּלְעָ֖ם עִם שָׂרֵ֥י בָלָֽק

verses.restored: Balak heard that Balaam had come and went out to meet him at city of Moab on border of Arnon, at end of border.

familiar.text: And when Balak heard that Balaam was come, he went out to meet him unto a city of Moab, which is in the border of Arnon, which is in the utmost coast.

modern.text: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע בָּלָ֖ק כִּ֣י בָ֣א בִלְעָ֑ם וַיֵּצֵ֨א לִקְרָאת֜וֹ אֶל עִ֣יר מוֹאָ֗ב אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל גְּב֣וּל אַרְנֹ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַגְּבֽוּל

verses.restored: Balak said to Balaam, Did I not surely send to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I truly not able to honor you?

familiar.text: And Balak said unto Balaam, Did I not earnestly send unto thee to call thee? wherefore camest thou not unto me? am I not able indeed to promote thee to honour?

modern.text: And he said to Balaam, “Did I not send you an urgent summons? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to richly reward you?”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בָּלָ֜ק אֶל בִּלְעָ֗ם הֲלֹא֩ שָׁלֹ֨חַ שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ לִקְרֹא לָ֔ךְ לָ֥מָּה לֹא הָלַ֖כְתָּ אֵלָ֑י הַֽאֻמְנָ֔ם לֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל כַּבְּדֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Balaam said to Balak, Look, I have come to you. Now, am I able to speak anything at all? Word Divine puts in my mouth, that I shall speak.

familiar.text: And Balaam said unto Balak, Lo, I am come unto thee: have I now any power at all to say any thing? the word that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speak.

modern.text: “See, I have come to you,” Balaam replied, “but can I say just anything? I must speak only the word that God puts in my mouth.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר בִּלְעָ֜ם אֶל בָּלָ֗ק הִֽנֵּה בָ֨אתִי֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ עַתָּ֕ה הֲיָכ֥וֹל אוּכַ֖ל דַּבֵּ֣ר מְא֑וּמָה הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָשִׂ֧ים אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּפִ֖י אֹת֥וֹ אֲדַבֵּֽר

verses.restored: Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.

familiar.text: And Balaam went with Balak, and they came unto Kirjathhuzoth.

modern.text: So Balaam accompanied Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בִּלְעָ֖ם עִם בָּלָ֑ק וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ קִרְיַ֥ת חֻצֽוֹת

verses.restored: Balak sacrificed cattle and flock and sent to Balaam and leaders who were with him.

familiar.text: And Balak offered oxen and sheep, and sent to Balaam, and to the princes that were with him.

modern.text: Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and he gave portions to Balaam and the princes who were with him.

original.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֥ח בָּלָ֖ק בָּקָ֣ר וָצֹ֑אן וַיְשַׁלַּ֣ח לְבִלְעָ֔ם וְלַשָּׂרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: In morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal, and from there he saw edge of people.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the morrow, that Balak took Balaam, and brought him up into the high places of Baal, that thence he might see the utmost part of the people.

modern.text: The next morning, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the outskirts of the camp of the people.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח בָּלָק֙ אֶת בִּלְעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲלֵ֖הוּ בָּמ֣וֹת בָּ֑עַל וַיַּ֥רְא מִשָּׁ֖ם קְצֵ֥ה הָעָֽם

translation_notes: Balak's fear follows Israel's recent victories; it explains the diplomatic crisis but does not justify antisemitic portrayals of Jewish people as an engulfing threat.
Balaam is a foreign diviner who nevertheless receives speech from YHWH; Divine communication is not portrayed as ethnically confined.
The narrative deliberately preserves tension between Divine permission in verse 20 and anger in verse 22; motives, persistence, and the restriction to speak only YHWH's word require literary audit.
The messenger stands as a satan/adversary in the ordinary Hebrew sense, not necessarily the later proper-name figure.
The donkey sees danger before the seer and speaks against repeated violence. The story plainly exposes animal cruelty and Balaam's impaired perception.
Payments of divination and curse-for-hire belong to the narrative; this is not instruction for magical practice.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 22 to promote curses, paid divination, antisemitic fear, animal abuse, or violence toward those who obstruct us. The donkey's perception and protest expose the blindness of coercive power, while Balaam is repeatedly forbidden to speak beyond the word given.
